claims.text: Elevated-temperature wear instability in FeNiCrCoCu coatings is driven by a thermally activated shift from dislocation-mediated plasticity to shear-induced atomic disordering.
The critical temperature is reached when thermal energy overcomes the stacking-fault-energy barrier.
Crossing the stacking-fault-energy barrier collapses ordered short-range-order clusters that stabilize the lattice.
The FeNiCrCoCu coating has a stable solid-solution microstructure at 300 K.
The FeNiCrCoCu coating has a high elastic modulus at 300 K.
The FeNiCrCoCu coating has a low dislocation density at 300 K.
Nanoindentation and reciprocating friction above approximately 600 K induce high-strain shear deformation in the coating.
At low temperature, FeNiCrCoCu plasticity is primarily mediated by edge-dislocation motion.
Lattice distortion and short-range order stabilize low-temperature dislocation-mediated plasticity in FeNiCrCoCu.
Severe lattice distortion reduces dislocation mobility in NbTaTiV.
Increasing temperature reduces the stacking fault energy in FeNiCrCoCu.
Thermal activation and shear break down unlike-atom pair correlations in FeNiCrCoCu.
High-strain compression induces a clustering-to-ordering transition in Al0.1CrCoFeNi, with increased unlike-atom pair correlations.
High shear stress combined with loss of short-range order produces a thermo-plastic instability.
Atomic disordering causes rapid lattice softening and loss of wear resistance in FeNiCrCoCu.
Above the critical temperature, FeNiCrCoCu exhibits a sharp decline in both wear resistance and elastic modulus.
Above the critical temperature, shear bands with high atomic disorder form and deformation shifts toward shear-induced amorphization or rapid lattice softening.
The estimated threshold is informed by an approximately 840 K spinodal temperature in Al0.1CrCoFeNi.
Increasing temperature produces a general thermal-softening trend in high-entropy alloys.

contradictions.description: The proposed mediator is loss of short-range order and disordering, but the mechanism characterizes this as similar to the cited Al0.1CrCoFeNi clustering-to-ordering transition. Ordering and disordering are opposite structural directions, and no argument is supplied that connects them.
